title: Trans-Sodium Crocetinate Ameliorates High-Altitude Acute Lung Injury via Modulating EGFR/PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB Signaling Axis.
authors: Liang, Keke; Ta, Yanlin; Xu, Liang; Ma, Shuhe; Wang, Renjie; Xiao, Chenrong; Gao, Yue; Li, Maoxing
one_liner_zh: 该文研究药物TSC通过EGFR/PI3K/AKT/NF-kB通路缓解高原肺损伤，虽含分子对接与动力学模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Saffron, a traditional Chinese medicine, is renowned for its pharmacological effects in promoting blood circulation, resolving blood stasis, regulating menstruation, detoxification, and alleviating mental disturbances. Trans-crocetin, its principal bioactive component, exhibits significant anti-hypoxic activity. The clinical development and therapeutic efficacy of trans-crocetin are limited by its instability, poor solubility, and low bioavailability. Conversion of trans-crocetin into trans-sodium crocetinate (TSC) enhances its solubility, stability, and bioavailability, thereby amplifying its anti-hypoxic potential. METHODS: This study integrates network pharmacology with in vivo and in vitro validation to elucidate the molecular targets and mechanisms underlying TSC's therapeutic effects against high-altitude acute lung injury (HALI), aiming to identify novel treatment strategies. RESULTS: TSC effectively reversed hypoxia-induced biochemical abnormalities, ameliorated lung histopathological damage, and suppressed systemic inflammation and oxidative stress in HALI rats. In vitro, TSC mitigated CoCl(2)-induced hypoxia injury in human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells (HPMECs) by reducing inflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress, and ROS accumulation while restoring mitochondrial membrane potential. Network pharmacology and pathway analysis revealed that TSC primarily targets the EGFR/PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB signaling axis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations demonstrated stable binding interactions between TSC and key components of this pathway. ELISA and RT-qPCR confirmed that TSC significantly downregulated the expression of EGFR, PI3K, AKT, NF-kappaB, and their associated mRNAs. CONCLUSIONS: TSC alleviates high-altitude hypoxia-induced lung injury by inhibiting the EGFR/PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB signaling pathway, thereby attenuating inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and restoring mitochondrial function. These findings highlight TSC as a promising therapeutic agent for HALI.
abstract_zh: 目的：藏红花作为一种传统中药，以其促进血液循环、化瘀、调经、解毒及缓解精神紊乱的药理作用而闻名。反式藏红花素（trans-crocetin）是其主要的生物活性成分，具有显著的抗缺氧活性。然而，反式藏红花素的临床开发及疗效受限于其不稳定性、溶解性差及低生物利用度。将反式藏红花素转化为反式藏红花素钠（trans-sodium crocetinate, TSC）可增强其溶解性、稳定性及生物利用度，从而放大其抗缺氧潜力。方法：本研究整合网络药理学与体内外验证，阐明TSC对高海拔急性肺损伤（HALI）治疗作用的分子靶点及机制，旨在识别新的治疗策略。结果：TSC有效逆转了缺氧诱导的生化异常，改善了肺组织病理损伤，并抑制了HALI大鼠的全身性炎症及氧化应激。在体外，TSC通过减少炎症细胞因子、氧化应激及ROS积累，同时恢复线粒体膜电位，减轻了CoCl(2)诱导的人肺微血管内皮细胞（HPMECs）缺氧损伤。网络药理学及通路分析揭示，TSC主要靶向EGFR/PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB信号轴。分子对接及动力学模拟显示，TSC与该通路关键组分之间存在稳定的结合相互作用。ELISA及RT-qPCR证实，TSC显著下调了EGFR、PI3K、AKT、NF-kappaB及其相关mRNA的表达。结论：TSC通过抑制EGFR/PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB信号通路，减轻炎症反应、氧化应激并恢复线粒体功能，从而缓解高海拔缺氧诱导的肺损伤。这些发现凸显了TSC作为HALI潜在治疗药物的前景。
